header.one_liner: DRDO-ADE is a core Indian UAV development laboratory behind indigenous unmanned-aircraft programmes.

what_it_is.prose: DRDO's Aeronautical Development Establishment is identified in government material as a key UAV development laboratory. PIB records ADE's role in developing TAPAS/Rustom-II, while the live UAS directory links ADE as a company/lab node.

deployments_procurement.summary: DRDO's Aeronautical Development Establishment is identified in government material as a key UAV development laboratory. PIB records ADE's role in developing TAPAS/Rustom-II, while the live UAS directory links ADE as a company/lab node.

import_dependencies.summary: No indigenous percentage or component import share is asserted without direct disclosure.

dimensions.label: Critical component sovereignty
dimensions.note: Active seeker indigenous; FPGA/GaN imported; propellant indigenous

dimensions.label: Export potential
dimensions.note: Armenia reported as Akash Mk-I export customer 2025; Akash-NG export potential not yet articulated

faq.question: What does ADE do?
faq.answer: It develops UAV systems including TAPAS/Rustom-II.

faq.question: Is ADE an Indian company?
faq.answer: No; it is a DRDO laboratory.

faq.question: What is TAPAS/Rustom-II?
faq.answer: An indigenous MALE UAV programme developed by ADE with HAL-BEL production partners.

sources.title: Successful Maiden Flight of Rustom-II
sources.note: ADE designed and developed TAPAS 201/Rustom-II with HAL-BEL production partners.
